rows.en:
The Film Research Society was allowed to use the audiovisual room after school.
It couldn't become an official club yet, you see, so it had no club room of its own.
He began editing with practiced hands.
"Today, as a special treat, I'll show you a new scene before it's been edited.
The climax is ferocious, but you'll have to wait for the finished film to enjoy that."
Then he pulled one reel out of the mountain of film piled up there.{p}

"...I haven't edited this one yet.
Let's watch this one today."{p}

The clapperboard filled the screen, and the acting began.
Take after take was called off, the same scene repeating again and again.
It's fascinating, you know.
"...Ah!"{p}
"...That's me on there.
I have to stop it!

I have to stop it, now!"
I had no idea at all what he was panicking about.{p}
Tokita was frantically trying to stop the editing equipment.
He should have been used to handling machines like that, yet maybe his fingers were shaking, because he didn't seem able to work it properly.{p}
"It won't stop... The machine won't stop!"

His face had gone deathly pale.
Startled, I looked back and forth between the screen and his face.{p}

On the screen were Tokita and the mummy.
"...That's amazing.
That's a really well-made mummy."
I honestly thought so.
It didn't look fake at all. It was as realistic as the real thing.{p}

"It's going to kill me!
If I don't stop it fast, the mummy's going to kill me!
Everyone dies.
Everyone who gets attacked in this film really dies!"
Tokita screamed in a trembling voice.
Honestly, I didn't understand.
It was at that moment.
He told me the secret of this film.
If someone told you something like that, could you believe it?
I'm sorry, but I couldn't.
People dying exactly the way it happened in a film? Surely not.
On the screen, Tokita was quaking with terror.
Just like the real one standing right in front of me...
"Eeeeek!"{p}

At last, he yanked out the plug.
But what do you think happened?{p}

The editing equipment was still running.
Even though he had pulled the plug.
"Aaaah!"
He clutched his head and crouched down right where he stood.
The Tokita on the screen was doing exactly the same thing.
After all, Tokita was the only one who knew the film's scenes.
I thought he was trying to scare me, so I did my best to stay calm.{p}

But it was right then.
Suddenly, a hand covered in bandages thrust out of the darkness and seized Tokita by the neck.
I couldn't do a thing.
It was all too much. I could only stand there, frozen.
Then, after the bandaged hand, a mummy with bandages wound around its face emerged from the darkness.
The eyeballs peering out between the roughly wound bandages were dull and clouded, like a dead fish's.{p}

"AAAAAAAAAGH!"
Tokita's death scream echoed through the audiovisual room.{p}

The mummy's hand gripped Tokita's head and crushed it.
The mummy crushed Tokita's head as easily as a mandarin orange.
What was left of Tokita, changed beyond recognition, looked like a split watermelon.
Even with his head crushed, Tokita's body was still twitching and trembling.{p}

I couldn't do anything. I just stood there.
When I suddenly came to my senses, the mummy was gone.
It had vanished, as if it had melted into the darkness.
All that was left behind was Tokita's corpse.{p}
And the editing screen showed Tokita lying dead in exactly the same pose, stopped on that very scene.
I ran.{p}
...Say, {a}.{p}Would you want to see that film?
I'd like to see it
I don't want to see it

I see.
I thought so.
You like horror films, after all.
You'd want to see just how incredible the footage on it was, I'm sure.
But you know, Tokita's death at school caused quite a stir, and yet the dozens of reels of film in the audiovisual room vanished without a trace, as if they had never been there at all.{p}

And with Tokita's death, the Film Research Society was disbanded too.
None of the Film Research Society's members knew anything about that film.
What was that film, I wonder?
If that film has been completed somewhere, I'd very much like to see it...{p}
By the way, I ended up taking one reel of that film with me.
Would you like to see just this one reel, at least?
I'd love to see it
I don't need to see it

I see.
But this is the one thing I can't show you.
The truth is, that scene was so incredible it was burned into my eyes, so I went to the trouble of buying an 8mm projector and watched it at home.
It was all there, clear as day.
The sight of Tokita being killed, just as I saw it with my own eyes.{p}

After that, I started watching the film at regular intervals.
As if I were observing it.
As the months went by, Tokita turned completely into a skeleton.
And before I knew it, there was no one on the screen anymore.
The bones were cleanly gone too, whether they'd crumbled away or someone had cleared them up.
Not a single bone was left.
Just the empty audiovisual room, shown flatly, on and on.
But when I looked closely, it wasn't so.
I was wrong to think no one was there.
Right beside the spot where Tokita's body had been, someone was standing there, blankly.{p}

...It was me.
As if it were reenacting what happened that day.
And behind me, an eerie bandaged hand was just about to reach out.
I hurriedly stopped the projector.
I wondered what I would do if it didn't stop, but luckily, it did.
That's why I'm still alive here today.
When I think of what would have happened if the machine hadn't stopped, like that time in the audiovisual room... it still makes my blood run cold.
That's why I will never watch that film again.
If I did, it would surely be my turn to die.
I can't bring myself to throw it away either, so I keep it carefully at the back of a drawer.{p}

All the while wondering what I'd do if someone ever watched it.
The terror of always living side by side with death... none of you could understand that, I suppose.
...That's how it always is for me.
Because of that living film.
Whether it's the mummy's curse or the film's curse, I can't tell.{p}

But what became of the film that disappeared back then?
Is it still passing from hand to hand, even now?
Maybe the reason people die is really no more than that.
Somewhere, someone quietly watches the footage of the moment you die.
It's a cursed film, after all.{p}

Perhaps it has changed its form.
Not 8mm film anymore, but a videotape...
And perhaps it has found its way into your home.
If you ever find an old videotape with no title label on it, be careful.
There's no guarantee that it's a tape of yours...
And with that, I'll end my story.{p}

I see.
To think there'd be another French-film lover here...
That's right.
French films choose their audience.
Even among my film-loving friends, only two or three people can understand that poetic world.
Which makes you, {a}, one of those precious few.{p}
By the way, {a}, what other kinds of films do you like?{p}

...You dislike them?
I see. That's a shame.
French films do choose their audience, after all.
Whenever I ask people if they like French films, they all tell me the images are beautiful.
But most of them say they can't understand what the film is about, or what's so interesting about it...
Sadly...
By the way, {a}, could it be that you dislike films altogether?{p}

Well, well...
This is a golden opportunity to make another French-film lover.
There are all sorts of French films, you know.
Some don't go over well with ordinary audiences, but others have popular appeal.
Next time, I'll pick out some French films I recommend for you.
You have my guarantee.
You're sure to love them.{p}
By the way, {a}, what kinds of films do you like?{p}

You dislike them?
I think films are wonderful things, myself.{p}

If it's the usual sort of film, then...
Today, let me tell you about a student at this school named Tokita.{p}

He was the kind of student who would stay up all night watching films and then doze off at school.
It wasn't that the teachers never scolded him, but Tokita's grades were decent, so they mostly let it slide.
No matter how much you love films, there's only so much you can buy or rent on a high schooler's allowance.
So he recorded TV broadcasts himself, and asked friends who had satellite or cable TV at home to tape things for him.
Well, the friends who had gladly agreed at first gradually started finding it a hassle.
Still, maybe it was down to Tokita's good nature.
His friends only made half-joking snide remarks, and kept recording for him.
Then, one day...{p}

"Huh? There's no title..."
A few times before, he had borrowed tapes where someone had forgotten to write the title.
Each time, not knowing what was on them had driven him crazy.{p}This time too, he couldn't stop wondering about it.
Hurry home and check it
Check it in the audiovisual room

Curious about what was on it, he hurried home.
And once he got home, he checked the tape.{p}

The tape showed nothing but ordinary scenes of the school.
Tokita assumed it was a home video someone had shot.
"I'll ask around whose it is and give it back."
A film or a TV recording is one thing, but with home video footage, you feel guilty, as if you were peeking into someone's diary.
Thinking that, he put it in his bag.{p}

The next day at school, he asked the people who had recorded for him about the tape.
But none of them recognized it.
Tokita was at a loss, and searched hard for the owner.
Well, most people would just think it was fine to wait for someone to come forward.
I suppose that's why nobody ever disliked Tokita.
But in the end, the owner was never found.{p}

Then he went home.
Even at home, he couldn't stop thinking about the tape.
"Maybe if I watch what's on it, I'll find out whose it is."
Once he thought that, he was seized by the temptation to see what was on it.
He was so into films, after all, so maybe it was only natural that a devil would whisper to him to watch it.
Maybe there was a film recorded after the home video scenes he'd seen yesterday.
The more he imagined things like that, the more his desire to watch it swelled up inside him.
And at last, he put the video into the deck and decided to watch it.{p}

The footage showed the school grounds, the same as yesterday.
"Huh, I'm in this."
On the screen was Tokita himself, looking for the videotape's owner earlier that day.
"But this tape got mixed in with mine yesterday..."{p}

The video went on, and night fell.
"That's weird. It should still be light outside."
When he looked at his window, the evening sun was streaming in.
Tokita realized he had been assuming the video was shot today, and found it funny.
"How dumb can I be? There's no way this was shot today."
And the footage rolled on.{p}

Some kind of white figure appeared.
"Who's that?"
Tokita followed the footage.
The figure gradually grew clearer.{p}

"A mummy man... So this was a film after all?"
By now, he was in the mood for watching a film.
He was watching the cruel scenes unfolding on the video with an appreciative eye.
He had already broken free of the delusion that it was real footage of today.
Then the video ended.{p}

For a while, Tokita just sat there in a daze.
Because amid the clumsy direction, scenes with a force like nothing he had ever seen had unfolded.
The mummy man had chased a high school girl and mercilessly torn her apart until she died.
"It must be an indie film.
If the school is the setting, someone connected with the school must have made it."
Once he thought that, he couldn't rest until he had found the tape's owner.
He wanted to see what came next... no, he wanted to see the finished film. With that thought, he went to bed.
And it was already starting to get light by the time he finally drifted off to sleep.{p}

Then, keeping his eyes on the ground, he hurried toward his classroom.
It was just as he was about to enter the school building.{p}

Lying in a corner of the ground there was a scrap of bandage.
At that moment, Tokita understood.
The footage on that video had really happened.
And from then on, he couldn't get the scenes from that video out of his head.
Apparently the police investigated the murder as the work of a deranged person.
But Tokita alone was certain the truth of the case lay elsewhere.{p}

He went home and sat thinking in front of the video.
That tape had gotten mixed in with his the day before yesterday.
But the incident must have happened last night.
Then what was it that had been recorded on that tape?
Still, no matter how he thought about it, it had to be a scene of last night's murder.
I have to check, he thought.
And he played the video once more.{p}
A figure came into view.{p}

And then, the mummy man.
"Huh.........?"{p}
